# Resource: stripe_topup

A top-up of your Stripe balance from your bank account. Set `status` to `canceled` to cancel a top-up that is still pending. Stripe moves a pending top-up to `succeeded` by itself. Only `description` and `metadata` change after creation.

~> A topup can move real money. In a live-mode Stripe account, creating or changing one, including setting its `status`, fails at plan time unless the provider sets `allow_live_money_movement = true`. Reading or importing one never does. The provider asks Stripe for the account's mode. See the Managing Test Data guide.

~> Stripe cannot delete a top-up; set `status` to `canceled` to cancel a pending one. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace the topup, fail at plan time. To stop managing a topup, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Add test funds to the balance from the account's bank account.
resource "stripe_topup" "funds" {
  amount      = 100000
  currency    = "usd"
  description = "Test funds"
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `amount` - (Required) A positive integer representing how much to transfer. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `currency` - (Required) Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies). Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.

The following arguments are optional:

* `description` - (Optional) An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users. Default: none.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`. Default (Stripe): `{}`.
* `payment_method` - (Optional) The ID of a PaymentMethod representing the payment method to be used for the top-up. A PaymentMethod of type `us_bank_account` can be used. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `payment_method_options` - (Optional) Payment method-specific configuration for this top-up. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`payment_method_options`](#payment_method_options) below.
* `source` - (Optional) The ID of a source to transfer funds from. For most users, this should be left unspecified which will use the bank account that was set up in the dashboard for the specified currency. While testing, this can be a test bank token (see [Testing Top-ups](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/testing#testing-top-ups)). Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. The provider keeps this value from configuration, because the conformance suite has not yet proven what Stripe returns for it. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `statement_descriptor` - (Optional) Extra information about a top-up for the source's bank statement. Limited to 15 ASCII characters. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Default: none.
* `status` - (Optional) The status of the top-up is either `canceled`, `failed`, `pending`, `reversed`, or `succeeded`. Possible values: `canceled`. Removing it from the configuration stops sending it, and the next apply records the value Stripe holds.
* `transfer_group` - (Optional) A string that identifies this top-up as part of a group. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Default: none.

<a id="payment_method_options"></a>
### `payment_method_options`

The `payment_method_options` attribute supports:

* `us_bank_account` - (Optional) If this top-up is to be used with a `us_bank_account` payment method, this sub-hash contains configuration for it. See [`payment_method_options.us_bank_account`](#payment_method_options.us_bank_account) below.

<a id="payment_method_options.us_bank_account"></a>
### `payment_method_options.us_bank_account`

The `payment_method_options.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `network` - (Required) The US bank transfer network used for this top-up. The default is `ach`. Possible values: `ach`.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `balance_transaction` - ID of the balance transaction that describes the impact of this top-up on your account balance. May not be specified depending on status of top-up.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `expected_availability_date` - Date the funds are expected to arrive in your Stripe account for payouts. This factors in delays like weekends or bank holidays. May not be specified depending on status of top-up.
* `failure_code` - Error code explaining reason for top-up failure if available (see [the errors section](https://docs.stripe.com/api/errors) for a list of codes).
* `failure_message` - Message to user further explaining reason for top-up failure if available.
* `initiated_by` - Indicates whether the top-up was initiated by Stripe or by the user. Possible values: `stripe`, `user`.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Removing from State

To stop managing a topup whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_topup.funds

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_topup.funds
```

The topup stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a topup using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_topup.funds
  id = "tu_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_topup.funds
  identity = {
    id = "tu_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the topup.

Using `terraform import`, import a topup using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_topup.funds tu_123
```
